h1: Ahrefs vs Semrush: priced in rupees, judged on Indian SERPs
metaTitle: Ahrefs vs Semrush: Priced and Tested for India
metaDescription: Ahrefs vs Semrush, priced in rupees and judged on Indian SERP data. Where both under-report Hindi and city keywords, and which one you should buy.
answer: Ahrefs and Semrush land within a few hundred rupees of each other once you add card forex and GST — roughly ₹11,500–₹12,700 a month at entry and ₹22,000–₹23,000 at the tier a working agency needs. Buy Ahrefs for backlink depth, Semrush if you also run Google Ads. Both under-report Hindi volume.
takeaways: The dollar sticker price is not the price. Add a **2–3.5% card forex markup**, then check your GST position — the gap between the two tools is smaller than the gap between what you budgeted and what your card statement says.
For English head terms in India both are usable. For **Hindi, Hinglish and tier-2 city long-tail**, both are systematically thin, and neither will tell you so.
Ahrefs is generally the stronger backlink index. Semrush is the broader suite — paid search, position tracking across many projects, social.
If you're two people and you do link work, buy Ahrefs. If you're two people and half your revenue is Google Ads, buy Semrush. Nobody needs both at ₹22,000 each.
A free stack of Search Console, Keyword Planner, Bing Webmaster Tools and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools genuinely covers most of the job. What it doesn't cover is competitor backlink research.

sections.h2: The short version, feature by feature
body: Both tools have been converging for a decade. Ahrefs added keyword and site audit tooling; Semrush rebuilt its backlink index. The remaining differences are real, narrower than either company's marketing suggests, and here's how they split on the work an Indian team actually does week to week.

callout.title: What neither of them is
callout.body: Neither tool is a source of truth for your own site. Search Console is. A rank tracker tells you what a robot in a data centre saw; Search Console tells you what a human in Indore actually clicked. See [GA4 vs Search Console](/compare/ga4-vs-search-console) for which of your own dashboards to trust.

sections.h2: What they actually cost in rupees
body: Both companies price in US dollars. Your bank does not. The number that matters is the landed cost — list price, plus the forex markup your card issuer charges on a foreign transaction, plus GST on that markup, plus whatever your GST position does to the invoice itself.
Most Indian cards charge **2% to 3.5%** on foreign currency transactions, and 18% GST applies to that markup fee. A few forex-friendly cards charge close to zero. Check yours before you assume.

bullets: **Ahrefs moved to a credit model.** Rows, reports and exports draw down a monthly allowance. A cheap plan you exhaust on day nine is not a cheap plan.
**Semrush's add-ons are the real cost.** The base plan is the entry fee; local, trends and AI toolkits are billed on top, per month.
**Annual billing saves roughly two months** on both. It also locks you in for a year, which is the wrong trade if you're still deciding.

**GST:** as an imported digital service, 18% applies. A GST-registered business accounts for it under reverse charge and claims input credit, so the net cost is close to the landed number. If you're not registered, add 18% and mean it. Confirm your own position with your CA — not with a blog post.

callout.title: Watch your annual foreign spend
callout.body: Foreign remittances above a threshold attract TCS under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, and the treatment of international card spends has been revised more than once. If your agency's tool stack plus ad spend runs into lakhs a year, that's a question for your accountant, not for the internet.

sections.h2: Where both tools go blind: Hindi, Hinglish and city long-tail
body: This is the part that matters most in India and gets written about least. Keyword volume in both tools is modelled — built from clickstream panels, Google Ads data and extrapolation. That model is only as good as its sample.

The sample skews English, urban, desktop and browser-extension-installed. Which means Devanagari queries, transliterated Hinglish (`sasta seo service`, `ghar ke liye solar panel price`) and tier-2 city modifiers are under-sampled by construction. You will routinely see zero or no-data against queries that are obviously being searched, because the panel never saw them.

The failure mode is not that the tools lie. It's that a zero looks identical to an absence, and a junior strategist builds a content plan around the English terms because those are the ones with numbers next to them.
The fix is boring and it works: treat both tools as a starting hypothesis, then verify against sources that see real Indian queries.
numbered: **Google Keyword Planner** — free with an active Ads account. Ranges are wide unless you're spending, but it sees Hindi and regional queries the panels miss.
**Your own Search Console query report** — the single most under-used keyword tool in India. Filter to queries with impressions and near-zero clicks. Those are pages you already half-rank for.
**Google Trends** — useless for absolute volume, excellent for relative interest between a Hindi term and its English equivalent, and for seasonality.
**Ask five customers what they typed.** Not a joke, and free. Indian buyers search in phrasings no keyword tool has a row for.

callout.title: The expensive mistake
callout.body: Ignoring a keyword because a tool shows 0 volume. In Indian-language and tier-2 markets, low reported volume plus visible SERP competition usually means the tool can't see the demand — not that the demand isn't there. We cover the practical side of this in [SEO in Hindi and Indian languages](/journal/seo-in-hindi-and-indian-languages).

sections.h2: Backlink index depth on Indian domains
body: Ahrefs runs one of the most active crawlers on the open web, and its link index is the reason most agencies keep paying. Semrush closed a lot of that gap after rebuilding its index, but on smaller and newer domains — which is most of the Indian web — Ahrefs still tends to surface links Semrush hasn't crawled yet.

Where both struggle is the long tail of Indian publishing: regional-language news sites, city directories, association pages, PDF press releases hosted on a college server. These get crawled slowly by everyone, so a genuinely useful link from a Marathi trade publication may not show up in either tool for weeks. Two consequences follow — don't judge a link vendor on what appeared in Ahrefs this week, and don't assume a competitor's link profile is complete.

Whichever tool you buy, treat its authority score as a sorting device, not a target. [DA and DR are different metrics from different vendors](/compare/da-vs-dr), neither is used by Google, and optimising for one is how agencies end up buying links on sites with a strong score and no readers.
bullets: **Referring domains, not backlinks.** One site linking a thousand times is one endorsement. Both tools default to the bigger, dumber number.
**Check the link, not the score.** Open five referring pages. If they're a template with unrelated text and an outbound link block, that's a network, and it will cost you later.

sections.h2: Which one a two-person team should actually buy
body: At ₹22,000-odd a month each, buying both is a ₹5.4 lakh annual line item for a two-person shop. That is a junior hire. Pick one.
The decision isn't really about the tools. It's about which half of the job you sell.

callout.title: The seat-sharing question
callout.body: Both vendors prohibit sharing a single seat between people, and both enforce it with session and IP checks. Two-person teams do it anyway and get locked out at the worst moment. Budget the second seat or accept the risk knowingly.

sections.h2: The free and cheap stack that covers most of it
body: Before you commit ₹2.7 lakh a year, be honest about what you'd use. For most small teams, roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of the daily job runs on tools that cost nothing.
What the free stack genuinely cannot do is competitor backlink analysis at depth and multi-client rank tracking at scale. Everything else is negotiable.
bullets: **Google Search Console** — free, and the only true record of your own queries, clicks and average position.
**Bing Webmaster Tools** — free keyword research and site audit on Bing's own data. Underrated because it isn't Google.
**Ahrefs Webmaster Tools** — free backlink data and site audit for domains you verify. It's Ahrefs' index, for your own site, at zero.
**Google Keyword Planner** — free with an Ads account, and the best free read on Indian-language demand.
**Screaming Frog** — free to 500 URLs, which covers a great many Indian SME sites entirely.
**Cheaper paid tiers** — SE Ranking, Mangools, Serpstat and similar sit in the ₹2,500–₹9,000/mo band. Weaker link indexes, perfectly adequate rank tracking and keyword research.

subs.h3: What we run, and why we say so
body: We pay for tools because we run [SEO retainers from ₹75,000/mo](/pricing) and the link research has to be defensible. That's a cost of doing our job, not a recommendation for yours. If you're a founder doing your own SEO on a ₹40,000 budget, half of it on a subscription is the wrong allocation — spend it on writing and on fixing the site. The tool doesn't rank anything. It tells you where to point the work.

versus.verdict: For a small Indian team whose deliverable includes links, buy Ahrefs; if you also run Google Ads or track rankings for eight-plus clients, Semrush earns the near-identical rupee cost — and if neither is true yet, run the free stack for 60 days first.

faqs.q: Is Ahrefs or Semrush better for Indian keywords?
faqs.a: Neither is good enough on its own. Both model search volume from clickstream panels that under-sample Hindi, Hinglish and tier-2 city queries, so you'll see zeroes against terms that are genuinely searched. Semrush has the larger raw keyword database; for Indian-language demand, cross-check both against Google Keyword Planner and your own Search Console.

faqs.q: What does Ahrefs cost per month in Indian rupees?
faqs.a: At roughly ₹88 to the dollar plus a 3% card forex markup, Ahrefs Lite lands near ₹11,700/month and Standard near ₹22,600. Add 18% GST if you're not registered; if you are, it's reverse-charged and claimable. List prices change, so verify before you buy.

faqs.q: Can I run an SEO agency without paying for either tool?
faqs.a: For a while, yes. Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Keyword Planner, Google Trends, free Screaming Frog and Ahrefs Webmaster Tools cover most of the daily work. The wall you hit is competitor backlink research and rank tracking across many clients — that's the point where a paid seat starts paying for itself.

faqs.q: Which tool has more backlinks in its index?
faqs.a: Ahrefs is generally the stronger link index, particularly on smaller and newer domains, which describes most of the Indian web. Semrush narrowed the gap substantially after rebuilding its index. Both are slow to crawl regional-language publishers and small institutional sites, so judge link work over a quarter, not over a week.

faqs.q: Do these tools tell me whether my SEO agency is working?
faqs.a: No. They tell you what a crawler saw. Whether the work is paying is a question about qualified leads from organic search measured against the baseline you froze on day one. Rankings and tool dashboards are diagnostics — useful for explaining a change, useless as the thing you're buying.
